narrative.overview:
A dense, informative catalogue that looks like iOS itself. The system's own grounds, bars, segmented controls, menus, forms and selection lists carry the structure; the brand speaks only through one ember accent taken from the app icon and through how much the screen tells you at a glance. Posters, ratings, voice actings, seasons and percentages are the decoration: data sits on posters and in rows, not in marketing cards.

Since the user's decision of 2026-11-11 («боле нативные по гайдлайну iOS, без наворотов»), the world is native per the HIG with no hand-drawn chrome. Toolbar actions are bare SF Symbols that the system bar draws as buttons; back is the system back button with its edge swipe. Actions are `.borderedProminent` and `.bordered` buttons; choices are menu pickers, `Form` rows and lists with a trailing system checkmark. The cinematic Apple TV header (blurred art, white Play, glass buttons) is the rejected default for the title page.

Density is high but legible: an 8 pt grid, Dynamic Type text styles everywhere, monospaced digits wherever numbers line up, and layouts that restack at accessibility sizes instead of truncating.
keyCharacteristics: System backgrounds, system navigation, system controls; brand only in tint, type weight and content.
One accent, on interactive elements only; one accent-filled primary action per screen.
Data first: facts strip, poster badges, voice-acting rows with popularity and flags.
Dynamic Type through AX5 with layout restacking; monospaced digits for data.
Motion is short (0.2 s) and falls back to none or a crossfade under Reduce Motion.

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: The accent appears only on things you can tap or on the mark of a current choice. Nothing static is ember.

rules.name: The Fill Is Not The Tint Rule
rules.body: Accent-filled surfaces with white text use Ember Fill, never the tint; the dark tint is a text colour.

rules.name: The Text Style Rule
rules.body: Every size is a Dynamic Type text style; no fixed point sizes. At accessibility sizes, side-by-side layouts stack (poster above title, facts grid to two columns, fact rows to caption-over-value, chips to a column).

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: Numbers that sit in columns or update in place (ratings, percentages, episode progress) use monospaced digits.

rules.name: The System Depth Rule
rules.body: Only system bars, sheets and materials create depth; views add no shadows or hand-rolled blur.

dos: **Do** use system controls first: `.borderedProminent` for the one primary action, `.bordered` for the rest, menu pickers for choices, `Form` for input, selection lists with a trailing system checkmark.
**Do** fill the primary button with Ember Fill (AccentFill), never the tint, and give it a second line naming what it will play or save.
**Do** use spacing and radii from DesignTokens (4 / 8 / 16 / 24; 4 / 8 / 12) and add a token only when a second view needs the same number.
**Do** use Dynamic Type text styles and restack layouts at accessibility sizes; keep every control at least 44 pt.
**Do** use monospaced digits for ratings, percentages and progress.
**Do** honour Reduce Motion: 0.2 s ease animations become none, the poster wipe becomes a crossfade, shimmers stop looping.
donts: **Don't** draw circles, capsules, gauges or badges as control chrome; system border shapes and content clipping (avatars) are fine.
**Don't** put toolbar symbols in their own background circle or replace the system back button.
**Don't** use the accent on non-interactive elements or introduce a second accent hue.
**Don't** add shadows or hand-rolled blur; depth belongs to system bars and sheets.
**Don't** build the details page as a cinematic Apple TV header with blurred art, a white Play and glass buttons.
